findings.description: The 'data' bucket sets no ACL, has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, and the inline comment confirms it is intended to be public. It holds a customer master spreadsheet, so anonymous principals could read or list sensitive customer data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects such as customer-master.xlsx are stored without enforced SSE-KMS encryption.
No logging block is configured, so unauthorised access to this publicly reachable bucket containing customer data would leave no audit trail.
Versioning is not enabled while force_destroy is true, so objects overwritten or deleted by an attacker cannot be recovered and tampering leaves no prior version as evidence.
No bucket policy denies requests with aws:SecureTransport = false, so object data in this public bucket may be transmitted over cleartext HTTP.

findings.issue_category: sensitive data in public unencrypted bucket
findings.description: A customer master spreadsheet is uploaded into aws_s3_bucket.data, which is public and unencrypted, and the object itself specifies no kms_key_id or server-side encryption, exposing sensitive customer records.
The financials bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial records are stored unencrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured for a bucket holding financial data, leaving no audit trail of object access.
Versioning is disabled while force_destroy is true, so deletion or tampering of financial objects is irreversible and leaves no prior version.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so it relies solely on the private ACL; a later ACL or policy change could expose financial data with no guardrail.
The operations bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so its objects are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No logging block is defined, so there is no record of who reads or modifies objects in this bucket for forensic or audit purposes.
No public access block resource guards this bucket, leaving it dependent solely on the ACL setting to remain private.
The data science bucket defines no server-side encryption, unlike the logs bucket which uses KMS, so its data is stored unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for this bucket, so there is no defence-in-depth control preventing future public ACLs or policies.
The centralised log bucket uses the log-delivery-write ACL and has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block; ACL or policy drift could expose aggregated access logs from other buckets.
